pr_title: Add --watch flag to pr checks command
pr_body:
<!--
  Thank you for contributing to GitHub CLI!
  To reference an open issue, please write this in your description: `Fixes #NUMBER`
-->

Hello maintainers! 

I'm using GitHub for a lot of projects, and found myself in the same situation as explained in https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/3669

CI checks takes a long time to run, and manually refreshing the GitHub web interface is suboptimal.

Following the discussion in the linked issue, I added a `--wait` flag to `pr checks` command. When this flag is used, the command does not exit immediately but report on current check statuses and wait until the number of pending checks is 0.

[![asciicast](https://asciinema.org/a/442125.svg)](https://asciinema.org/a/442125)

Fixes #3669

Implementation wise this PR refactor the current `pr checks` code to extract the data gathering logic and splits the 3 "modes" (web mode, wait mode, single execution mode) to reuse the current functionalities in multiple places. Existing functionalities have not been modified.  

I did not work on the `--watch` as I think it requires a bit more discussion around the desired UI, while the `--wait` is useful to everyone having to wait for a slow CI with a simpler UI.  
With this command is possible to execute use cases like "merge after all checks have been successful" from the GitHub CLI.

Happy to receive feedback about this, there are possible improvements but I wanted to keep this focused on a single change.  
Thank you!
pr_comments: @endorama Thanks for the contribution! After discussing with the team offline we have come to the consensus that it would be confusing to have both a `--wait` and `--watch` flag for this command. We think having a `--watch` flag with a UI that refreshes in the same manner as `gh run watch` is the direction we want to go. From a quick glance at the PR it does look like many of the changes you made could be reused to pivot in this new direction, is that something you would be interested in working on? If not, can close this PR and allow other contributors to work on the issue?
Hi @samcoe, thank you for looking into this and sorry for missing the notification. I'll work on the `--watch` flag.

@samcoe I removed the `--wait` and added the `--watch` flag, copying the behaviour from `run watch` command.

There are 2 main differences:
- I used  a different ANSI escape code (`\033[H\033[2J` instead of `\x1b[2J`); this code properly clear the screen and reset position to 0,0 (at least on Linux but I can't run it on other platforms at the moment)
- I added `SIGINT` handling to exit with code `1` (still checks pending) or `0` (all checks completed; this is an edge case)

Let me know and thanks for the patience.

@endorama Thanks for the continued effort here. Two quick comments. 

> I used a different ANSI escape code (\033[H\033[2J instead of \x1b[2J); this code properly clear the screen and reset position to 0,0 (at least on Linux but I can't run it on other platforms at the moment)

The current code `\x1b[2J` is not working for you on Linux? If it is working I would suggest we continue to use it. If it isn't working we should change it in both places. 
cc @vilmibm Since you wrote `run watch` which uses that screen clearing code.

> I added SIGINT handling to exit with code 1 (still checks pending) or 0 (all checks completed; this is an edge case)

Seems to me that this mostly adds unnecessary complexity for a no real improvement. If the user manually cancels the command then they should get the SIGINT exit code.

I still got to do a full code review but just wanted to address those two changes you brought up.

> The current code \x1b[2J is not working for you on Linux? 

Is only partially working: this code only clears the screen without resetting the cursor to 0,0 position. 
This is visually strange, as the text is attached to the bottom of the terminal window, suggesting to scroll. I'll wait on some hints from @vilmibm about this.

> Seems to me that this mostly adds unnecessary complexity for a no real improvement. If the user manually cancels the command then they should get the SIGINT exit code.

I'll remove it.
@samcoe I did another round. I would wait for your review before moving on to refactoring `collect` and `printTable` as the direction for the `for {` wasn't perfectly clear to me.
@vilmibm I made the changes requested, can you please take another look 🙇

The [release notes for gh v2.5.1](https://github.com/cli/cli/releases/tag/v2.5.1) incorrectly say that a `--wait` flag has been added, whereas the flag is now named `--watch`.
Also this PR should probably be renamed to mention `--watch` instead of `--wait`.

issue_context.title: Add interactive mode to `gh pr checks`
issue_context.body:
I find myself quite frequently pushing a change, creating a pr and waiting for checks to complete... If the checks are a bit long, but not too long, I don't want to move on to another thing. So I keep spamming `gh pr checks` again and again waiting for them to be complete...

### Proposed solution

Add an option to the command such as `gh pr checks --wait`. If invoked like this, the command would show the checks but not exit immediately, rather it would wait until all checks are done (updating the cli output as they finish). Only then would it return to the shell.
comments:
Makes sense!

if `gh run watch` took a `--pull-request` argument, would that suffice for this usecase?

Hi,
I'm not sure that would work - I have 2 runs associated with each PR - `push` and `pull_request` - both of them need to finish for the PR to be marked as successful. So I am not sure `gh run watch` could be repurposed here, as it would need to possibly watch multiple runs :/ (maybe my implementation is strange, but I don't know how to get statuses per-push and per-PR without duplicates for my own PRs... So I'm probably not alone in this :D)

Thanks!

I would definitely want a `watch` command that works on a pull requests, like I think both of you are suggesting. I would show the status of each run associated with a PR. That would probably mean that it wouldn't have the level of detail that `gh run watch` has right now, but it's fine if it just shows the overall status of each run— sort of like `gh pr checks` does.

@marekdedic your usecase makes perfect sense!

I've got no argument against `gh pr checks --watch`.

review_comments: @vilmibm I changed this from `pr.BaseRefName` to `pr.HeadRefName`, let me know if that makes sense. This is the only functionality outside of `--watch` mode that was changed.
